LESSON: LENGTH

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.1: Length
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Length, part of Measurement in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Why do we measure distances inday to day life? 2. How do we use length in real life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Discuss in purposive groups/pairs and identify the millimetre as a unit of measuring length using a ruler. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication-(AAC) (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/ point/sign/write) during the discussion.

2. Measure length of objects in millimetres using a rule in purposive groups/pairs or as individuals. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any other alternative functional part of the body or assistive technology to measure lengths using adapted metre 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Discuss in purposive groups/pairs and identify the millimetre as a unit of measuring length using a ruler. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication-(AAC) (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/ point/sign/write) during the discussion.
2. Measure length of objects in millimetres using a rule in purposive groups/pairs or as individuals. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any other alternative functional part of the body or assistive technology to measure lengths using adapted metre 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Length together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: learner works amicably with peers to determine lengths in centimetres and millimetres in addition, subtraction,

multiplication and division and discuss the answers.
